title: Unified Eval Harness + Prompt Sets + Quantization + Regression Triage Playbook
author: Maya Rodriguez
summary: Comprehensive playbook describing the eval harness, prompt-set standards, benchmark SLOs, model onboarding checklist, quality guardrails, recommended quantization profiles, and regression triage process for Redwood Inference applied ML teams.
body:
Purpose
--------
This playbook documents the integrated Applied ML evaluation lifecycle used at Redwood Inference: how we design and run eval harness jobs, author and curate prompt sets and benchmarks, onboard models into serving, apply quality guardrails, select quantization profiles, and triage regressions. It is intended for ML engineers, model owners, and reliability engineers responsible for keeping served model quality within agreed thresholds.

Scope & Audience
----------------
- Scope: open and licensed models we serve (hosted/dedicated/private), developer-facing endpoints, and internal evaluation pipelines.
- Audience: ML engineers, applied ML researchers, SREs working on inference, and engineering managers approving rollouts.

Glossary
--------
- Eval harness: the CI/CD-integrated job that runs prompt sets and metrics against a model and records observable outputs.
- Prompt set: curated collection of inputs and expected behaviors used for benchmarking and regression detection.
- Guardrail: automated checks and thresholds that prevent low-quality model rollouts.
- Quantization profile: recommended precision and kernel choices for a model variant.
- Regression triage: defined process to investigate and remediate detected quality regressions.

Ownership & Roles
-----------------
- Model owner: primary contact for a model (create onboarding doc, maintain prompt sets).
- Eval owner (Applied ML): maintains shared eval harness infra and templates.
- SRE: ensures eval jobs run reliably and results are uploaded to metrics storage.
- Release approver (Product/ML): signs off on rollouts once guardrails are green.

Eval Harness Architecture (high level)
-------------------------------------
1. Source artifacts: model binary, config, prompt-sets, eval-config.yaml.
2. Orchestration: CI pipeline (buildkite / GitHub Actions) triggers an eval run for every model change or candidate rollout.
3. Execution: job launches evaluation containers on dedicated GPU pool; harness supports batching, temperature/seed sweeps, and deterministic KV-cache initializations.
4. Storage: outputs (responses, token-level latencies, logs) and metrics are pushed to the eval metrics DB (Influx/ClickHouse) and S3 artifact bucket.
5. Dashboarding: per-model eval dashboard with metric history, diffs, and regression annotations.

Design principles for eval harness
---------------------------------
- Determinism: seed control and fixed model config to enable repeatable comparisons.
- Cost-awareness: sample prompt frequency according to traffic-weighted importance.
- Explainability: store full model outputs for triage and human review.
- Automation-first: gate rollouts when guardrails fail; provide clear override process.

Prompt Sets & Benchmarking Guidelines
------------------------------------
- Prompt-set metadata (required for every set): name, owner, domain, intended-use, sample-size, difficulty, expected-behavior, tags.
- Construction rules: include positive/negative cases, edge cases, and adversarial examples. Prefer real anonymized customer examples for production workloads.
- Size guidelines: small triage sets (50-200), regression sets (200-2k), production benchmarks (2k-10k) depending on product impact.
- Partitioning: train/dev/regressions; label prompts with severity and behavioral expectations.

Example prompt-set metadata table:
| field | description | example |
|---|---:|---|
| name | unique id | customer-support-v2 |
| owner | person/team | maya-rodriguez (applied-ml) |
| domain | vertical | customer-support |
| expected_behavior | high-level | concise accurate answer w/ next-step suggestion |
| tags | categories | classification, safety |

Benchmark metrics (standardized across teams)
- Accuracy / F1 / EM (as applicable)
- Hallucination rate (manual + classifier-assisted) — target < 2% for high-risk flows
- Latency P50/P95 token-level and end-to-end — targets defined by product route (e.g., hosted-chat P95 < 450ms)
- Stop-token/format correctness for structured outputs — target 99.5%
- Safety flags per 1k prompts — threshold depends on route (sensitive routes < 1 per 10k)

Model Onboarding Checklist (must be completed before canary rollout)
1. Create model entry in model-catalog with unique model_id and tags.
2. Provide model card: architecture, training data summary, license, known limitations, contact.
3. Add canonical prompt sets: smoke, regression, production-benchmark.
4. Define quantization profiles and test performance for each (see Quantization Profiles).
5. Run eval harness: attach a full eval report with metric history and artifacts.
6. Review by Applied ML + Product owner; sign-off recorded in model-catalog.
7. Create rollback plan and health monitors (SLOs, error budget for quality metrics).

Quality Guardrails and Automated Gates
-------------------------------------
Guardrails are implemented as CI checks plus runtime monitors. A model fails the gate if any of the following occur during an eval run:
- Delta-based regressions: metric drop > defined delta (example: F1 drop > 3% absolute for critical routes).
- Hallucination increase: >50% relative increase or absolute > 2% (whichever triggers first).
- Latency regression: p95 increase > 20% or absolute p95 exceeds route SLO.
- Safety violations: any new safety class escalation in regression set.
- Format failures: structured outputs with schema validity < 99.5%.

Override policy: Manual overrides require triage notes, dual approver from Applied ML and Product, and an associated mitigation plan for observed regressions. Overrides are logged in the model-catalog release entry.

Quantization Profiles & Recommendations
--------------------------------------
- Profiles describe: precision (fp16/int8/4-bit), backend kernel family, caching policy, and expected memory / throughput tradeoffs.
- Guidelines by model size:
  - < 7B: prefer fp16 or 4-bit quantization (LLM.int4) when throughput is required; validate on dev benchmark.
  - 7B-30B: test int8/4-bit mixed with kernel optimizations; monitor for accuracy drift on semantic tasks.
  - >30B: start with fp16 or int8-fp16 hybrid; quantization must be validated on regression and safety sets.

Recommended quantization YAML example (eval config snippet):
---
model_id: gptx-cust-7b
quant_profiles:
  - name: q4_0_perchannel
    precision: int4
    kernel_family: fused-attn-v2
    expected_memory: "8GB"
    notes: "good perf/accuracy balance for short-context chat"

Validation matrix to run for each profile:
- Production benchmark (throughput + accuracy)
- Safety/regression set pass/fail
- Latency & concurrency stress test (95th pct under target load)

Regression Triage Playbook (step-by-step)
----------------------------------------
1. Detect: an eval run or runtime monitor flags a regression (auto-created incident in triage tracker).
2. Classify severity:
   - Sev 1 (blocking rollout / customer-impacting): major accuracy loss on production benchmark or safety violation.
   - Sev 2: localized degradation (single intent or format issue).
   - Sev 3: minor cosmetic or non-blocking metric drift.
3. Initial data collection (within 30 mins):
   - Attach failing prompts, model outputs (both new and baseline), metric diffs, and logs.
   - Run quick A/B comparison job (same seeds) using eval harness.
4. Triage owner (Model owner + Applied ML) reproduces regression and narrows root cause:
   - model-change? config/quantization? infra/kernel change? prompt drift?
5. Mitigation options (ordered):
   a) Rollback to last-known-good model variant (fastest).
   b) Use fallback routing to older model family for impacted route.
   c) Patch prompt/template and re-evaluate.
   d) Revert quantization change and re-run tests.
6. Postmortem: within 3 business days include timeline, root cause, corrective actions, and follow-ups. Link to postmortem doc in model-catalog.

Templates & CLI snippets
-----------------------
- Trigger an eval run (example):
  ./scripts/run_eval.sh --model-id gptx-cust-7b --prompt-set regression/customer-support --profile q4_0_perchannel --output s3://redwood-evals/2028-04-01/gptx-cust-7b/

- Minimal eval-config.yaml example:
  eval_name: nightly-regression
  model_id: gptx-cust-7b
  prompt_sets:
    - regression/customer-support
    - smoke/basic-behaviors
  metrics:
    - accuracy
    - hallucination_rate
    - latency_p95

Operational SLO examples (for eval harness + production monitoring)
- Eval-run success rate (CI): 99% monthly.
- Eval-run completion time: median < 45 minutes for production-benchmark 2k prompts.
- Regression triage SLA: initial classification and data collection within 30 minutes for Sev 1/2.
- Postmortem published within 3 business days for Sev 1 incidents.

Reporting & Dashboards
----------------------
- Per-model dashboard shows: baseline vs candidate diffs, time-series for key metrics, recent failing prompts, and rollout history.
- Weekly quality review: applied-ml + product review top regressions and approve scheduled rollouts.

References & Related Pages
------------------------
- Eval harness standards: /confluence/applied-ml-and-evals/eval-harness/applied-ml-eval-harness-standards-2025
- Quantization profiles: /confluence/applied-ml-and-evals/quantization-profiles/quantization-profiles-best-practices-2026
- Model onboarding examples and templates: /confluence/applied-ml-and-evals/model-onboarding/model-card-template

Change history
--------------
- 2028-04-01 (Maya Rodriguez) — initial published playbook.
- 2029-02-15 (Maya Rodriguez) — expanded quantization guidance for >30B models and clarified override policy.

Appendix: Example regression incident quick checklist
- Notify stakeholders (model-owner, applied-ml, sre)
- Snapshot failing outputs and baseline outputs (S3 path)
- Run targeted A/B eval with same seeds
- If rollback executed, confirm new traffic telemetry green for 1 hour before full resume

For questions or to request a new prompt-set or quantization experiment, ping #applied-ml on Slack or file an issue in the applied-ml trackers.
